context.requirement_text: ISS-0816 (queue task 816). CursorPage<T> declares a has_more field. The issue was filed on the premise that lib/letflow/audit.ex emits has_more on the wire, so one CursorPage<T> was covering two incompatible wire shapes. That premise was refuted by ISSUE-FIXER at Step 1 and the issue record docs/issues/ISS-0816.yaml carries the correction inline; the Step 1 audit, not the record, is authoritative. The real defect is that no Letflow route emits has_more at all, so CursorPage<T>.has_more covers zero wire shapes, and two frontend call sites fabricate the field client-side from Boolean(next_cursor). The fix is to delete the field, split the envelope along the axis the backend genuinely varies on (two-key {items, next_cursor} versus three-key {items, next_cursor, count}), retype every call site to the envelope its route actually emits, and record the route-to-shape mapping so it need not be re-derived.
context.source_text: Narrow re-gate of the amended design at commit 6a88623a (revision 2, rework iteration 1) on branch feature/WF03-ISS0816-20260925. Revision 1 was failed by this role at commit 2da52436 on two blockers, both in the T7 guard specification. CODE-DESIGNER closed both with a single change -- narrowing T7's regex from the bare token to the code forms of the field -- and applied four non-blocking corrections plus one newly found consequence (section 6.3 / T9, the ISS-0765 surface guards).

task.description: WF-03 Step 2b, rework iteration 1. Narrow re-gate of lib/letflow/design/iss-0816-cursorpage-has-more-audit.md at commit 6a88623a. The scope is deliberately restricted: claims (a) the refuted premise, (b) the two-key/three-key split, (e) the three docblocks and the TenantListResponse non-change, (f) the modulesApi weakest-claim decision, (g) the T8 bystander and the no-weakening property of adding a PATTERNS entry, and (h) out-of-scope discipline were all independently confirmed at the previous gate, claim (c)'s four-TS2353 measurement was re-measured to the character, and claim (d)'s scope-widening was upheld; none of those is to be re-derived here. Verify only that the two blockers raised at commit 2da52436 are genuinely closed and that closing them introduced nothing new. Specifically: (1) establish whether T7's three regex alternatives really do cover every way TypeScript can express the field -- property access, object-literal or type-member key including the optional has_more? form, and string-literal key -- and actively hunt for a form the regex misses, because a missed form is a hole in the very guard this fix exists to install. (2) Re-run the measurement independently in a throwaway git worktree with the new regex, confirming or refuting CODE-DESIGNER's reported results: 20 hand-built strings all classified correctly, then the full probe giving npm run guards at 52 tests passing with source-scan reporting zero violations while api.ts carries the prose section 4 requires and identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 stays untouched and unexempted, tsc -b at exit 0, and npm test at 890 passing. (3) Confirm that section 4's new authoring rule -- in prose, write the token inside backticks and never immediately followed by a colon -- is structurally sufficient given the regex, i.e. that a closing backtick is neither whitespace nor a colon so prose written to the rule cannot match. (4) Judge whether the accepted cost is the right trade and is stated rather than hidden: a bare has_more in prose, outside backticks and not followed by a colon, is no longer caught, on the argument that prose cannot make a request or type a response and that a guard policing prose is what created the first blocker. (5) Confirm section 8 item 8 is struck through rather than deleted, that the stated cause is accurate, and that the unfiltered grep figure of fourteen occurrences across eight files matches what is actually measured. (6) Confirm decision (c) is accurately restated on INV-D with the wrong-write-path framing explicitly withdrawn on the GroupMemberAddResult.created grounds raised at the previous gate, and that the conclusion still follows without the corruption claim. (7) Confirm the three minor corrections landed: pagination.ex:51, the truncated boundary specified in both directions, and section 10 naming ISS-0823. (8) Gate the new section 6.3 and T9: CODE-DESIGNER found that adding listAllMembers makes groupsApi a seventh function, which affects two ISS-0765 guards -- T-0765-SURFACE at identity.groupsApi.test.ts:229, an exact-equality assertion over Object.keys, and T-0765-NO-ADMIN-PREFIX's hand-maintained surfaceRows array. The design says both must be extended, not weakened, and states this was read verbatim from source and NOT measured, so measure it: confirm both guards exist as described, confirm they would in fact break, and confirm the extension is specified precisely enough that FRONTEND-DEV cannot satisfy it by loosening an ISS-0765 assertion, since a fix that quietly degrades the previous run's regression coverage is the real risk. Write the verdict to handoffs/WF03-ISS0816-20260925/step-02b-design-gate-rework1.json, run the single-file handoff lint on it, commit and push. Modify nothing outside handoffs/; all probing in a throwaway worktree. Work synchronously with no Monitor and no background wait, and take timestamps from date -u.

result.summary: FAIL, but a much narrower one than iteration 1. Both original blockers are genuinely closed -- measured, not read -- and everything else in the rework checks out. One new BLOCKER: the narrowed regex is correct on all 22 forms the design enumerates, but it does not cover ES6 shorthand property syntax, and that gap is not theoretical. I reintroduced the exact ISS-0816 defect into web/src/api/promotions.ts in shorthand spelling -- 'const has_more = Boolean(response.next_cursor)' followed by 'return { items, next_cursor, has_more }' in the same .then callback the fix is removing -- and BOTH gates passed it: source-scan clean, tsc -b --force exit 0. The tsc half is not a surprise, it is the finding from my own first gate, where promotions.ts:265 was measured NOT to error because the .then return position is not excess-property-checked. So T7 as specified fails to cover the one position where the type system provably cannot help, in the most idiomatic spelling, in the same file and function as the original defect. T7's stated purpose in section 7 is that has_more 'cannot reappear as a field in production source'; with shorthand uncovered, it cannot make that claim. The fix is one regex alternative and I have already measured a working replacement: adding '|\bhas_more\s*[,}]|\b(?:const|let|var)\s+has_more\b' closes all five shorthand forms with zero false positives across every prose form written to section 4's backtick rule and all four TimelineFeed forms, catches the reintroduced defect at promotions.ts:262, and leaves the real tree clean at 49/49. Related and directly connected: section 7.1's 'cost of narrowing, stated rather than hidden' paragraph names only the prose cost and omits the code-form cost entirely, so the design currently understates what the narrowing gives up. On the rest: BLOCKER-1 closed -- npm run guards 4 files / 52 tests all passing with source-scan at zero violations while api.ts carries section 4's required has_more prose at two lines. BLOCKER-2 closed -- identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 passes untouched and unexempted; the exemption set is exactly the two ISS-0821 files, both still writing the code form has_more: false, so both still genuinely need it. tsc -b --force exit 0 and npm test 125 files / 890 tests passing, matching section 8 items 10 and 11 exactly. Decision (c)'s restatement on INV-D is accurate and is a genuine improvement, with member_result_map/3 verified at lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:829-831 returning "created" => created?. All three minor corrections landed correctly. T9 measured: T-0765-SURFACE at :229 does break exactly as described, the stated extension fixes it, and the suite goes 16 to 17 tests green. One precision point on T9 that matters more than its severity suggests -- T-0765-NO-ADMIN-PREFIX does NOT break; it stays green and silently under-covers, because it_each iterates a hand-maintained array. The design's own wording ('must be extended', 'honouring that intent requires a row') is accurate and never claims otherwise, but an implementer who runs the suite, sees one red, and fixes only that will lose the coverage without any signal. Worth stating outright, given that silent coverage loss is the named risk.

blocking_findings.title: T7's narrowed regex does not cover ES6 shorthand property syntax, and the exact ISS-0816 defect can return through the gap past both tsc and the guard
blocking_findings.where: lib/letflow/design/iss-0816-cursorpage-has-more-audit.md section 7.1, the regex and its 'Three alternatives, one per way the field can actually be written in TypeScript' claim
blocking_findings.detail: The specified regex is /\.has_more\b|\bhas_more\s*\??\s*:|["']has_more["']/. Its three alternatives cover a property access, a colon-separated key, and a string-literal key. They do not cover ES6 shorthand, which is a fourth way TypeScript expresses the field and is not exotic -- it is what an agent or developer writes by default when a variable of the same name is already in scope. Five forms measured as MISSED: object-literal shorthand 'return { items, next_cursor, has_more }'; the declaration that feeds it, 'const has_more = Boolean(response.next_cursor)'; destructuring shorthand 'const { items, next_cursor, has_more } = page'; parameter destructuring 'function f({ items, has_more })'; and a semicolon-separated type member 'has_more' with no annotation. Note the asymmetry that shows this is an oversight rather than a decision: the RENAMED destructure 'const { has_more: hasMore } = page' IS caught, because it happens to contain a colon, while the plain shorthand that is strictly more common is not. Why this is blocking rather than pedantic: I reintroduced the defect the fix removes, in the same file and the same function, spelled with shorthand, and ran both gates. source-scan passed. tsc -b --force exited 0. The tsc result is not incidental -- at the first gate I measured that promotions.ts:265 does NOT produce a TS2353 because the .then callback's return position is not freshness-checked, which is precisely why the design classifies its removal as a clarity edit rather than a compile requirement. So the one position in this codebase where the type system is already known not to catch a fabricated has_more is also the position T7 does not catch it. Section 7's own statement of what T7 proves -- 'has_more cannot reappear as a field in production source' -- is not true as specified.
blocking_findings.measured: Probe worktree at 6a88623a with the full section 4/5/7.1 shape applied. (i) Regex classification: 22 of 22 enumerated forms correct, then 5 of 5 shorthand forms MISSED. (ii) Defect reintroduced into src/api/promotions.ts as 'const has_more = Boolean(response.next_cursor)' plus 'return { items: response.items, next_cursor: response.next_cursor, has_more }' inside the existing .then: npx vitest run tests/guards/source-scan.spec.ts -> 1 passed, zero violations; ./node_modules/.bin/tsc -b tsconfig.json --force -> exit 0. Both gates let the defect through.
blocking_findings.must_change: Extend the regex with a shorthand alternative. Measured working replacement, which I ran end to end: regex: /\.has_more\b|\bhas_more\s*\??\s*:|["']has_more["']|\bhas_more\s*[,}]|\b(?:const|let|var)\s+has_more\b/. Against the same corpus this gives 0 missed forms (all 22 enumerated plus all 5 shorthand) and 0 false positives across every prose form written to section 4's backtick rule and all four TimelineFeed forms; with it in place source-scan flags the reintroduced defect at web/src/api/promotions.ts:262 and reports zero violations on the clean tree, with meta-control and source-scan together at 49/49. The shorthand alternative is compatible with the backtick authoring rule by construction: in '`has_more`,' the character after the token is a backtick, which is neither whitespace nor a comma nor a closing brace, so backticked prose still cannot match. If a different formulation is preferred that is fine, but it must be measured against both the shorthand set and the prose set, not reasoned about -- reasoning about this regex is what produced the gap. Section 7.1's claim 'one per way the field can actually be written in TypeScript' must also be corrected, since it is the sentence that made the gap invisible.

blockers_from_previous_gate.title: Design section 4 required a docblock that T7's bare-token regex forbade
blockers_from_previous_gate.evidence: The narrowing makes section 4's prose legal. In the probe worktree I wrote section 4's required content into web/src/types/api.ts as real docblocks -- line 16 reads ' *  No Letflow route emits `has_more` -- the internal one from' and line 26 reads ' *  ONLY -- never a cross-page total. No Letflow route emits `has_more`. */' -- so the token appears twice in the single file the guard most needs to protect, exactly as section 4 demands. npm run guards (all four spec files) reported 4 files / 52 tests all passing, with 'source-scan > web/src/**/*.{ts,tsx,css} has no guard violations' green and all four has-more-wire-field meta-control assertions green. Zero violations. This is the direct refutation of the failure I measured at iteration 1, where the same probe produced 'has-more-wire-field @ web/src/types/api.ts:14'. CODE-DESIGNER's section 8 item 10 reports 52 tests and zero source-scan violations; I reproduce both exactly. The diagnosis behind the fix is also right: T7 was banning a word when INV-A is about a field, and the two rejected alternatives were correctly rejected -- exempting api.ts would have gutted the guard at its most important file, and rewording section 4 would have cost it the stated purpose of naming the field so the issue is not re-filed. Section 7.1 records both rejections with reasons, which is the right way to close a gate finding.

blockers_from_previous_gate.title: T7's exemption list omitted web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63
blockers_from_previous_gate.evidence: Under the narrowed regex the file needs no exemption at all, which is the stronger of the two possible fixes. web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 still reads ' *  No `has_more` -- Pagination.Page never emits one. */', it is not in allowedPaths, it is inside source-scan's src/**/*.{ts,tsx,css} glob, and source-scan reported zero violations. Measured, not inferred. The final exemption set is exactly the two ISS-0821 files, and I confirmed both still need exempting for a real reason rather than by inheritance: PromotionReviewListPage.test.tsx:119 and :270 and TaskInboxPage.test.tsx:134 and :160 all still write the literal code form 'has_more: false', which the narrowed regex correctly catches. Section 7.1 also states that the allowedPaths entry carries an inline comment saying the two exemptions are deleted when ISS-0821 lands, which keeps the exemption from outliving its cause.

independent_verification.item: (1) Regex coverage against the three enumerated ways TypeScript can express the field
independent_verification.verdict: CORRECT for the enumerated forms, INCOMPLETE overall -- see BLOCKER-3
independent_verification.evidence: All 22 forms I built behaved correctly under the specified regex: 12 must-match (has_more: boolean; has_more?: boolean; the real fabrication has_more: Boolean(response.next_cursor); a real DlqPage fixture literal; if (page.has_more); optional chain page?.has_more; non-null assert page!.has_more; page['has_more']; "has_more"; a newline between key and colon; a space before the colon; and the renamed destructure const { has_more: hasMore }) and 10 must-not-match (all four real prose comments in the tree, both docblock sentences section 4 requires, the backtick-then-colon prose form, and all four TimelineFeed forms -- the type member hasMore: boolean, the destructured hasMore, the JSX attribute hasMore={Boolean(...)}, and the guard {hasMore && (). Two details worth recording because they are non-obvious and correct: \s in JavaScript matches a newline, so a key split across lines is caught; and the optional-chain and non-null-assertion forms are caught by the property-access alternative because both retain the dot. The gap is ES6 shorthand, which is a fourth expression form the design does not enumerate. See BLOCKER-3.

independent_verification.item: (2) Independent re-measurement of the full probe
independent_verification.verdict: CONFIRMED -- all three of CODE-DESIGNER's reported results reproduce
independent_verification.evidence: Method: git worktree add --detach to a scratchpad path at 6a88623a, node_modules supplied by a directory junction, working checkout never touched. Applied the full shape myself rather than trusting the report -- section 4's two envelope interfaces with the required has_more prose, the EntityRecordsPage and GroupMemberPage aliases, all thirteen section 5.2 retypes across audit.ts / AuditLogPage.tsx / instances.ts / tasks.ts, section 5.4's full promotions.ts restructure removing the .then and its inline anonymous response type, the three DlqPage fixture keys, section 7.1's narrowed PATTERNS entry, and T8's two fixtures. Results: npm run guards (meta-control, source-scan, bundle-scan, role-set) -> 4 files, 52 tests, all passed, source-scan zero violations -- matches section 8 item 10 exactly, including the 48-to-52 delta being T8's four fixture assertions. ./node_modules/.bin/tsc -b tsconfig.json --force -> exit 0 -- matches item 11. npx vitest run --passWithNoTests --exclude tests/e2e/** --exclude tests/guards/** -> 125 test files, 890 tests, all passed -- matches item 11. CODE-DESIGNER's item 9 claim that 20 hand-built strings classified correctly is consistent with my own larger 22-string run, in which every enumerated form behaved as claimed.

independent_verification.item: (3) Section 4's backtick authoring rule -- structural sufficiency
independent_verification.verdict: SUFFICIENT for the alternative it addresses, INCOMPLETE for the other two
independent_verification.evidence: The stated rule is: in prose, write the token inside backticks and never immediately followed by a colon. Against the colon alternative \bhas_more\s*\??\s*: the rule is structurally sufficient, and the reasoning the design gives is right -- a closing backtick is neither whitespace nor a colon, so \s* cannot span it and the colon can never be reached. Measured: ' * `has_more`: never emitted by any route.' does NOT match, which is the hardest case for the rule since a colon does follow, just not immediately. But the rule addresses only that one alternative. Prose that names the field in a DOTTED form inside backticks -- ' * the old `response.has_more` fabrication is gone' -- MATCHES the property-access alternative, and prose that uses a QUOTED form -- ' * the wire never carried a "has_more" key' -- MATCHES the string-literal alternative. Both measured. Neither occurs in any prose section 4 or section 5 requires, so nothing is blocked today, but the rule exists precisely so a future author does not trip the guard, and as written it would not protect them. Recommend restating it as: write the token BARE inside backticks -- not dotted, not quoted, and not followed by a colon.

independent_verification.verdict: The trade is RIGHT; the statement of it is INCOMPLETE
independent_verification.evidence: On the merits the argument is correct and I endorse it. Prose cannot make a request or type a response; INV-A as amended is about declared and accessed fields; and a guard that policed prose is exactly what produced BLOCKER-1, so giving up prose coverage to buy back a guard that can coexist with honest documentation is a good trade. Stating it openly rather than letting it pass unremarked is the right practice and I would not want it removed. The problem is that section 7.1's paragraph presents prose as the WHOLE cost of narrowing -- 'A bare has_more in prose outside backticks and not followed by a colon is no longer caught. That is accepted: it is prose, it cannot make a request or type a response.' That is true of prose and false as a complete account, because the narrowing also gave up the shorthand CODE forms, which are not prose and which can very much make a request and type a response. So the paragraph currently names the harmless half of the cost and omits the harmful half. Once BLOCKER-3 is fixed the paragraph becomes accurate as written, which is another reason to prefer fixing the regex over redefining the cost.

independent_verification.item: (5) Section 8 item 8's withdrawal and its corrected figures
independent_verification.verdict: Withdrawal CORRECT and well done; the occurrence count CONFIRMED; the file count WRONG
independent_verification.evidence: The form of the correction is right: the false claim is struck through rather than deleted, the replacement names the specific cause (the grep -v __tests__ filter excluded files that T7, being appliesTo: 'source', does scan, because source-scan's glob is web/src/**/*.{ts,tsx,css} with no __tests__ exclusion), and it records both what iteration 1's bare-token regex actually measured and what the narrowed regex measures instead. Leaving the struck text visible is the right call -- it is what stops the same filtered grep being run again. On the figures: 'fourteen occurrences' is CONFIRMED -- grep -rn has_more over web/src with --include for .ts, .tsx and .css returns exactly 14. 'across eight files' is WRONG -- it is 7 files (types/api.ts 3, dlq/__tests__/DlqPage.pagination.test.tsx 3, api/promotions.ts 2, pages/promotions/__tests__/PromotionReviewListPage.test.tsx 2, pages/tasks/__tests__/TaskInboxPage.test.tsx 2, api/audit.ts 1, api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts 1). 8 files is the count only when web/tests/ is included, and that scope gives 15 occurrences rather than 14, so the sentence takes its occurrence count from one scope and its file count from another. web/tests/e2e/obs04.timeline.e2e.spec.ts is outside source-scan's src/** glob, so the guard-relevant figure is 14 across 7. Minor, but this is the paragraph whose entire purpose is to replace a bad measurement with a good one, so it should be exact.

independent_verification.item: (6) Decision (c) restated on INV-D, with the wrong-write-path framing withdrawn
independent_verification.verdict: CONFIRMED accurate, and a genuine improvement
independent_verification.evidence: The withdrawal is explicit and correctly grounded: section 3(c) now carries a 'Deliberately not claimed: state corruption' paragraph citing GroupMemberAddResult.created at web/src/types/api.ts:498-502 and, newly, the backend builder member_result_map/3. I verified that new citation -- lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:829-831 is exactly '@spec member_result_map(String.t(), String.t(), boolean()) :: map()' at :828 with 'defp member_result_map(group_id, user_id, created?) do' at :829 and '%{"group_id" => group_id, "user_id" => user_id, "created" => created?}' at :830 -- so the idempotency claim is now evidenced on both sides of the wire, which is stronger than what I asked for. The conclusion does still follow without the corruption claim: the dropdown is a different control from the member list and is derived from the truncated set rather than displaying it, so a notice over the list leaves the dropdown presenting missing members as addable. That argument never depended on the write being destructive. INV-D was also generalised from 'a list dialog that computes a set difference' to 'a control that is derived from a fetched collection -- a set difference, a count, an availability check', with an explicit note that it does not depend on any claim about corrupted writes. That generalisation is correct and makes the invariant reusable, and it now covers ISS-0823 as the same class, which section 10 says. Nothing overstated remains.

independent_verification.verdict: ALL THREE CONFIRMED applied and correct
independent_verification.evidence: pagination.ex line number: section 3(c) now reads 'lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:51 @default_page_size 50', and :51 is correct (@max_page_size 200 at :50, @default_page_size 50 at :51). The truncated boundary: section 6.1 now specifies it in both directions and states the principle behind it -- truncated reports whether members were left unfetched, not whether the cap was reached, so a 20th response with next_cursor null yields truncated false (a group of exactly 4 000 members is complete, not truncated) while a non-null next_cursor at the cap yields true, and no 21st request is issued either way. A new T5b was added to test the boundary case, and OQ-2 was amended to say the behaviour at the cap is no longer an open question. That is a more complete fix than the one-sentence clarification I asked for. Section 10: the '(unfiled)' row now names ISS-0823 with the queue task, GH issue and commit, and I confirmed docs/issues/ISS-0823.yaml exists with matching title, discovered_by CODE-DESIGNER, discovered_in_run WF03-ISS0816-20260925 and severity MINOR.

independent_verification.item: (8) Section 6.3 and T9 -- the ISS-0765 surface guards
independent_verification.verdict: Both guards CONFIRMED to exist as described and the extension CONFIRMED to work; one framing point needs stating outright
independent_verification.evidence: Measured rather than read, since the design itself flags section 6.3 as read-from-source-but-not-measured. Both guards exist verbatim. T-0765-SURFACE is at identity.groupsApi.test.ts:229 -- citation exact -- and asserts Object.keys(groupsApi).sort() toEqual an exact six-element array. T-0765-NO-ADMIN-PREFIX drives it.each over surfaceRows, whose comment does say it 'must enumerate EVERY surviving function, so that adding a seventh one with a bad prefix is caught without anyone remembering to write a bespoke row for it'. Step 1: I added listAllMembers to groupsApi per section 6.1's contract and ran the file. T-0765-SURFACE FAILED -- 'AssertionError: expected [ addMember, create, ...(5) ] to deeply equal [ addMember, create, ...(4) ]', reported at line 229 -- exactly as the design predicts. T-0765-NO-ADMIN-PREFIX did NOT fail: all six of its cases stayed green, because it.each iterates a hand-maintained array and a seventh function on the object simply never produces a seventh case. Result 1 failed, 15 passed. Step 2: I applied the design's stated extension verbatim -- inserted 'listAllMembers' between 'list' and 'members' in the :229 array, and added ['listAllMembers', () => groupsApi.listAllMembers('g-1')] to surfaceRows. Result 17 passed, 0 failed, and the new case 'T-0765-NO-ADMIN-PREFIX: groupsApi.listAllMembers does not dial /api/v1/admin/' passes. So the extension is correct and the coverage is genuinely restored, 16 tests to 17. Two details in the design that I verified rather than assumed: the stated sort position is right -- 'list' sorts before 'listAllMembers' because it is a proper prefix, and 'listAllMembers' before 'members' on l versus m -- and the claim that the existing spy lets the row work unchanged is right, because installSpy(WIRE_MEMBER_PAGE) returns next_cursor null so the drain terminates after one request and the URL assertions apply to that single call. On whether FRONTEND-DEV could satisfy T9 by loosening: the design gives concrete positive instructions with exact contents and positions, says in bold that both must be extended and not weakened, and states that neither is a defect, so there is no reason to reach for a loosening move and core-directives.md's 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures' covers it globally. The residual risk is not the instruction, it is the measurement I just made: only ONE of the two goes red. An implementer who runs the suite, sees a single failure at :229, fixes it and moves on has silently dropped the surfaceRows row, and nothing anywhere will say so. The design's own wording never claims both fail -- it says 'must be extended' and 'honouring that intent requires a row', which is accurate -- but the sentence 'ISS-0765 left two assertions that pin the surface at six' reads as though both would break, and surfaceRows does not pin anything. Given that quiet degradation of ISS-0765's coverage is the named risk here, section 6.3 should say plainly that T-0765-NO-ADMIN-PREFIX will stay GREEN and silently under-cover, and that the row must therefore be added deliberately rather than in response to a red test.

issues.description: T7's narrowed regex misses ES6 shorthand property syntax. Five forms measured as uncaught, including 'const has_more = Boolean(response.next_cursor)' and 'return { items, next_cursor, has_more }'. I reintroduced the exact ISS-0816 defect into web/src/api/promotions.ts in that spelling, in the same .then callback the fix removes, and both gates passed it: source-scan clean, tsc -b --force exit 0. tsc cannot help in that position -- that is the promotions.ts:265 finding from the first gate -- so T7 is the only guard there and it does not fire. A measured replacement regex that closes all five forms with zero false positives is given in result.blocking_findings BLOCKER-3.

Section 7.1's 'The cost of narrowing, stated rather than hidden' paragraph is incomplete. It names the prose cost only and omits the shorthand code-form cost, so the design currently understates what the narrowing gives up. Directly connected to BLOCKER-3; fixing the regex makes the paragraph accurate as written.

Section 4's authoring rule is incomplete. 'Write the token inside backticks and never immediately followed by a colon' is structurally sufficient against the colon alternative -- measured, a closing backtick is neither whitespace nor a colon -- but it does not address the other two alternatives. Prose using a dotted form inside backticks ('`response.has_more`') matches the property-access alternative and a quoted form ('"has_more"') matches the string-literal alternative; both measured. Neither occurs in any required prose today. Recommend: write the token BARE inside backticks -- not dotted, not quoted, not followed by a colon.
